name: Complete student engineering workflow with verification
covers: actual Earth-to-spacecraft scale ratio and visual exaggeration disclosure
description: Verifies the primary engineering workflow remains connected after subsystem model hardening.
steps: Open Orbital Lab
Inspect Payload including focal length and detector pitch
Open Spacecraft and inspect battery, thermal and communications assumptions
Open Orbit & Maneuver and inspect transfer ΔV
Open Simulation and run the scenario
Open Engineering Analysis, Verification and Design Report
expected: All workspaces are reachable; GSD, ADCS, power, thermal, communications and propulsion checks show explicit results and fidelity assumptions.

name: Reject invalid engineering inputs
description: Verifies invalid engineering values do not silently become plausible results.
steps: Open Orbit & Maneuver
Enter an invalid eccentricity or altitude
Open Verification
expected: The Engineering inputs valid check reports FAIL instead of silently accepting the invalid design.

name: Ground track and solar terminator seasonal calibration
description: Checks the day/night boundary and night mask render on the equirectangular ground-track map for all four seasonal calibration epochs.
steps: Open Simulation and locate the 2D Ground Track map
Set Solar overlay epoch to Vernal equinox and confirm two pole-to-pole vertical terminator lines plus night shading on the hemisphere opposite the sub-solar point
Set Solar overlay epoch to Summer solstice and confirm the terminator reaches approximately 66.56° N and 66.56° S, with the North Pole inside the daylight region
Set Solar overlay epoch to Autumnal equinox and confirm the two vertical meridians return
Set Solar overlay epoch to Winter solstice and confirm the terminator reaches approximately 66.56° N and 66.56° S, with the South Pole inside the daylight region
Confirm the cyan ground-track line remains visible above the night shade and is still split at the antimeridian
expected: All four epochs display a continuous, correctly clipped terminator and night mask; equinoxes show two vertical meridians without pole-spanning spikes, solstices show the expected ±66.56° terminator limits and correct polar illumination.

name: Satellite tracking TLE validation and pass prediction
description: Verifies the satellite tracking workspace can use a live catalog or pasted TLE and predict station visibility windows.
steps: Open Satellite Tracking in the RUN navigation group
Refresh the live TLE catalog or paste a complete three-line TLE
Set station coordinates and minimum elevation
Click Predict next 24 hours
Paste a malformed TLE and verify validation feedback
expected: A valid TLE shows SGP4 look angles and pass rows with AOS, peak elevation/time, LOS and duration; invalid inputs show a visible error without crashing.

name: Satellite Ops sky path and radio Doppler estimate
covers: ground station and current satellite markers
description: Checks the original tracking view visualizes a selected pass and updates the first-order Doppler estimate from the configured frequency.
steps: Open Satellite Tracking
Load a valid satellite TLE
Enter a positive nominal radio frequency
Predict the next 24 hours
Inspect the world map with the current subsatellite point, station marker and upcoming SGP4 ground track
Inspect the 24-hour pass timeline and select a pass from its visual bar
Select a predicted pass and inspect the polar sky path
Change the nominal frequency and inspect the Doppler estimate
expected: The world map renders antimeridian-safe future ground-track segments plus current satellite and station markers; the 24-hour timeline displays and selects predicted passes; the polar sky plot and first-order Doppler estimate update without controlling radio hardware.

name: Catalog group selection and pass export on mobile
covers: mobile navigation opens only on demand
mobile navigation closes after section selection
description: Verifies mobile navigation behavior alongside catalog selection, filtering and pass export.
steps: Open the mobile navigation menu and verify it is hidden before tapping the menu control
Select Satellite Tracking and verify the menu closes and the tracking workspace appears
Choose a different catalog group and wait for data status
Filter the object list by a name fragment
Run pass prediction for a valid object
Export the resulting pass table to CSV
expected: The mobile menu stays hidden when closed, uses a compact two-column layout when opened, and closes after Satellite Tracking is selected; the selected catalog group loads or shows a clear network error, filtering narrows the object selector, and a successful prediction enables CSV export.

name: Earth 3D space environment and mobile mission-control view
covers: selected spacecraft telemetry remains tied to the propagated state
description: Verifies the Earth-Moon-only 3D view supports system framing, touch navigation, and model changes without changing the selected orbit or telemetry.
steps: Open the Earth 3D workspace on a mobile viewport
Choose SYSTEM and verify Earth and Moon are both framed with the lunar orbit visible
Use a two-finger pinch gesture to zoom in and out, then drag to orbit the camera
Change the spacecraft model from the selector and verify its silhouette changes
Return to TRACK and verify spacecraft telemetry and propagated orbit remain unchanged
expected: The Earth-Moon system is framed, pinch and drag controls respond, spacecraft silhouette changes on selection, and the selected mission state and telemetry remain unchanged.

name: Mission analysis backend returns validated orbital metrics
covers: EME2000 position and velocity state vectors
description: Verifies mission analysis uses the independently hosted Orekit engine and clearly discloses its two-body fidelity.
steps: Open Mission Analysis
Use the default orbit inputs
Set propagation time to 600 seconds
Click Run analysis
Inspect the orbital metrics, propagated epoch, EME2000 position/velocity and engine integration status
expected: Finite orbital metrics and state vectors appear; Orekit 13.1.9 and the connected Orekit HTTP adapter are identified; the TAI epoch advances by 600 seconds; the page discloses two-body fidelity and that GMAT/STK/FreeFlyer remain future adapters.

name: Mission analysis rejects an Earth-intersecting orbit
description: Verifies invalid orbital geometry is rejected with a visible message and no plausible-looking result.
steps: Open Mission Analysis on a mobile viewport
Set altitude to 120 km and eccentricity to 0.99
Click Run analysis
expected: A visible validation error explains that the periapsis intersects Earth and no result metrics are shown.
